hooks.text: A secret radioactive clock is bolted to the side of Voyager.
NASA electroplated pure uranium-238 onto the covers of the Voyager records.
A 4.5-billion-year atomic clock is speeding out of our solar system.

title: The Radioactive Clock Bolted to Voyager
description: The Voyager Golden Record carries an ultra-pure sample of uranium-238 to tell extraterrestrials how old it is. Here is how NASA built a billion-year atomic clock for deep space.

beats.text: A secret radioactive clock is bolted to the side of Voyager.
beats.visual: artist concept of Voyager 1 spacecraft cruising through interstellar space, NASA, 2013

beats.text: In 1977, NASA launched twin robotic probes into space, carrying identical gold-plated phonograph records as time capsules for extraterrestrial civilizations.
beats.visual: photograph of the Voyager Golden Record mounted on the spacecraft, NASA, 1977

beats.text: The recordings hold natural sounds of thunder and whale songs, spoken greetings in 55 languages, and Ann Druyan's brainwaves while falling in love.
beats.visual: photograph of the golden phonograph record groove surface, NASA, 1977

beats.text: Committee chair Carl Sagan even added a pulsar map locating our solar system relative to 14 pulsars.
beats.visual: diagram of the pulsar map etched on the Voyager Golden Record, NASA, 1977

beats.text: To protect the records, engineers fitted an aluminum cover electroplated with an ultra-pure sample of uranium-238, which has a half-life of approximately 4.5 billion years.
beats.visual: close-up diagram of the aluminum cover for the Voyager Golden Record, NASA, 1977

beats.text: By measuring that radioactive decay, any finder can read the record's precise age, deciphering how long ago Earth sent its cosmic message.
beats.visual: artist concept of Voyager spacecraft in interstellar space with Golden Record visible, NASA, 2012
